events.name: Schools for colored children in Philadelphia (Abolition Society report, 1838)
events.description: The 1838 Abolition Society report counted every school for colored children in Philadelphia: 1,116 scholars on the rolls of the free schools, 226 in schools part free and part pay, 102 in pay schools under white teachers, and 288 in ten pay schools taught by colored teachers, among them Sarah M. Douglass, David Ware and Solomon Clarkson. || The report: 'much labor has been bestowed upon them, in order to effect an improvement, which we confidently believe has been attended with some degree of success. But although it is admitted that too much neglect is still attributable to the parents in respect to sending their children to school, we believe it is a fault which all who are conversant with public schools, will acknowledge to be equally chargeable to indigent persons, whether white or colored.' THE TABLE (figures in order: on the roll, attending, in rudiments, reading, reading and writing, cyphering and grammar, geography, higher branches; a dash is a blank in the table; blanks at the end of a row are left off): FREE SCHOOLS: Northern Liberties Public School (220, 84, 64, 37, 15, -, 11, -); Lombard Street public school, boys (200, 150, 80, 120, 40, 60, 11, 22); Lombard Street public school, girls (263, 160, 193, 70, 100, 40, 30, 25); Locust Street Infant School (120, 80, 80); Adelphi Infant School (90, 63, 63); Tidmarsh Infant School (82, 65, 65); Adelphi, boys (88, 60, 15, 40, 65, 28, 22, 4); Bray's (12, 10, 12); Shelter for Colored Orphans (41, 41, 41); Total (1,116, 713, 613, 267, 220, 128, 74, 51). PART FREE AND PART PAY: Willing's Alley, boys (72, 45, 24, 48, 44, 38); Willing's Alley, girls (82, 40, 12); Clarkson, girls (72, 40, -, 65, 64, 54, 3, 1); Total (226, 125, 36, 113, 108, 92, 3, 1). PAY SCHOOLS, UNDER CARE OF WHITE TEACHERS: Mount Zion Church, Is. Corbet (17, 14, 7, 6, 4); Elizabeth Street, Abigail Brown (35, 30, 20, 10, 10, 10); Clarkson H[all] Sch[ool], boys, G. Luther (50, 45, -, 50, 50, 45, 45, 30); Total (102, 89, 27, 66, 64, 55, 45, 30). PAY SCHOOLS, TAUGHT BY COLORED TEACHERS: David Ware (45, 37, 20, 20, 15, 9, 2); Solomon Clarkson (40, 40, 10, 30, 30, 12); Susan Powell (8, 8, 8, 8); Emeline Brown (22, 22, 14, 8, 1); Ann Eliza Carey (30, 25, 23, 7, 3, 3, 5); M. and S. Gordon (30, 25, 10, 20, 20, 10, 10); Sarah M. Douglass (43, 38, 4, 40, 28, 37, 21); Eliza Matthew (33, 33, 8, 25); Eliza Ann Rolley (12, 12, 1, 11, 8, 8); Eliza West (25, 20, 17, 8, 1); Total (288, 260, 115, 177, 106, 79, 38). The column totals in this transcription match the printed totals. The white teachers (Is. Corbet, Abigail Brown, G. Luther) are named here as text only. M. and S. Gordon are Martha B. Gordon and Sarah Ann Gordon of 57 Pine Street (Sarah Ann was one of Arthur Donaldson's scholars in 1813). Source: Pennsylvania Society for Promoting the Abolition of Slavery, The Present State and Condition of the Free People of Color, of the City of Philadelphia and Adjoining Districts (Philadelphia, 1838; read January 5, 1838), page 29, courtesy the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/presentstatecond00penn/page/29/mode/2up). Michiko Quinones's photograph of the page: clippings/PAS_1838_p29_schools-for-colored-children.jpg
